--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.select_last_edges_created()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select the last N edges that were created. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.select_last_edges_created()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Select the last N edges that were created. title: >- [Graph.select_last_edges_created()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Select the last N edges that were created. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select the last N edges that were created. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23663-L23753){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.select_last_edges_created( n, set_op="union", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select last edges created](/assets/graphs/select-last-edges-created.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node grid whose seven edges are labeled 1 to 7 in the order they were created. select_last_edges_created(2) selects the two most recent, D–E and E–F, drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Selects the `n` most recently created edges. The graph keeps track of the order in which edges were added (see `get_edge_creation_order()`), and this method takes the tail of that order. Edges that have since been deleted are skipped. This is useful in incremental workflows where a step adds a batch of edges and the next step needs to act on just that batch, for example to: - assign a weight, type, or timestamp to the edges just added with `set_edge_attrs_ws()` - roll back the last few additions with `delete_edges_ws()` - inspect what a generator or a `fully_connect_nodes_ws()` call produced with `get_edge_df_ws()` Selection is based on creation order, not on edge IDs. The edges are added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise, and any node selection is cleared. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of most recently created edges to select. Must be a non-negative integer (a negative value raises `ValueError`). If `n` is larger than the number of edges, every edge is selected; `n=0` selects nothing. [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How these edges combine with the current edge selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected edges among them, and `"difference"` removes them from it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The four edges of this path are created in order, so selecting the last two picks out `C-D` and `D-E`: ::: {#f08df38e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) .select_last_edges_created(n=2) ) [ (graph.get_label_from_id(e.source), graph.get_label_from_id(e.target)) for e in (graph.get_edge(eid) for eid in sorted(graph.get_selected_edge_ids())) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('C', 'D'), ('D', 'E')] ``` ::: ::: A batch of edges added later can be tagged without touching the original ones. Here two "late" edges are added and marked, so the edge table shows `late` only on the last two rows: ::: {#e03098c1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( graph .clear_selection() .add_edge("A", "C") .add_edge("C", "E") .select_last_edges_created(2) .set_edge_attrs_ws(late=True) ) graph.get_edge_df().select("id", "source", "target", "late") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
